pass_a_gloss: To Abraham indeed once it had been said by God: go out from your land; but to us perhaps after a little it will be said: go out from the whole land; to whom it is fine to be persuaded, so that he quickly may point out to us the heavens, in which is the so-called kingdom of the heavens. About many virtues then it is possible to see life filled with contests and those competing. For they will seem, about moderation, others too besides those from the share of God to have competed, many, and with manliness some to have died in it, keeping the purpose on behalf of the common master, and those clever about examined arguments to have taken care of practical wisdom, and those having proposed to live justly to have given themselves to justice. And against each virtue campaigns either the mindset of the flesh or also the many of the outside things; but about godliness only competes the picked-out race, the kingly priesthood, the holy nation, the people for acquisition, the rest of humans not showing, not even as far as seeming, that, if there are things competing against the godly, they purpose to die on behalf of godliness, honouring before the death with godliness the living with ungodliness. And each of those wanting to be from the picked race is persuaded to hear God saying at every time, also when those being godless under pretext of being many-godded plot against him, the: there will not be to you other gods except me, and the: name of other gods you will not recall in your hearts, nor will it be named out of your mouth. For which reason by heart God is believed by such to justice, and by mouth confessed by such to rescue, they grasping that neither will they be made just unless they so trust God, their heart being so set, nor will they be in rescue unless of what sort the disposition is, of such sort is also the word. For they cheat themselves, those thinking it suffices for gaining the end in Christ the: for by heart it is believed to justice, even if there is not added the: and by mouth it is confessed to rescue; and it is possible to say that it is more to honour with the lips having the heart far off from God than to honour him with the heart, the mouth not confessing to rescue.
pass_b_english: Abraham was once told by God, “Go out from your land” (Genesis 12:1); and to us, perhaps, it will soon be said, “Go out from the whole earth.” It is good to obey him, so that he may quickly show us the heavens, in which is what is called the kingdom of heaven.

Now one can see that life is full of contests over many virtues, and one can see those who contend in them. For many people other than those of God's portion will be thought to have contended for self-control; some will be thought to have died with courage, holding to their resolve on behalf of their common master; those skilled in arguments that are put to the test, to have cultivated prudence; and those who have set themselves to live justly, to have given themselves to justice. Against each virtue there fights either “the mind of the flesh” (Romans 8:7) or else most of the things outside us. But for piety only “the chosen race, the royal priesthood, the holy nation, the people for God's own possession” (1 Peter 2:9) contends, while the rest of mankind do not show, even in appearance, that if there are forces that fight against the pious, they are resolved to die for piety, preferring death with piety to life with impiety.

Each of those who wish to belong to the chosen race is convinced that he hears God saying at every moment, even when those who are godless under the pretext of having many gods are plotting against him: “You shall have no other gods besides me” (Exodus 20:3), and “You shall not call to mind the name of other gods in your hearts, nor shall it be named from your mouth” (Exodus 23:13). So by such people God is believed “with the heart unto righteousness” and confessed “with the mouth unto salvation” (Romans 10:10), since they grasp that they will not be justified unless they believe God in this way, with their heart so disposed, nor will they be in salvation unless their word is of the same kind as their disposition.

For those deceive themselves who think that, for attaining the goal in Christ, “for with the heart one believes unto righteousness” is enough, even if “and with the mouth one confesses unto salvation” is not added to it. Indeed one may say that it is more a case of honouring God with the lips while keeping the heart far from him (Isaiah 29:13) than of honouring him with the heart, when the mouth does not confess “unto salvation”.
